   2003]. In Vinaya legal analysis, the commentary and the *Parivāra* identify this rule—beginning with "lying down together"—as an example of an *acittaka* offense, wherein a monk can incur a transgression blamable by ordinance (*paṇṇattivajja*) unintentionally (*asañcicca*) [Harvey].
This training rule is widely attested across early Buddhist monastic traditions. SuttaCentral records direct parallels in the Prātimokṣa and Vibhaṅga recensions of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Dharmaguptaka, Mahāsāṅghika, and Kāśyapīya lineages preserved in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan, alongside the corresponding rule for nuns (*Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya* 102) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse data from DharmaNexus reflects extensive internal parallels with Vinaya *khandhaka* texts (such as the *Bhesajjakkhandhaka*, *Mahākhandhaka*, and *Senāsanakkhandhaka*) and suttas like the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), as well as cross-language alignments with Tibetan Vinaya literature, including the *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* and Gunaprabha's *Vinayasūtravṛtti* [DharmaNexus].
